claim: For a normalized positive sum of projections H, complement LCU gives a polynomial-circuit isometry V and a diagonal one-sparse projection B with H <= V*BV = 2H-H^2 <= 2H on the full logical space.
quantifiers: Every finite projection list with positive normalized weights; exact algebraic gate model for the specified circuit.
costs: Polynomial label size and circuit size from the term generator; B has one nonzero per computational row and O(log M) label locality. Exact algebraic rotations are assumed; finite-gate synthesis errors are not charged.
boundary: This does not supply polynomial row enumeration for C=I-VV* or prove quantum PCP.

claim: For the legal BMVZ-admissible hard family augmented by two forced BJSW singleton seed layers, every exact PREPARE completion of the complement-LCU construction has max computational-basis row support of C0=I-VV* at least ceil(5^R/D), where R is the repeated-block count and D is the padded label dimension.
quantifiers: All unitary A with the specified first column chi; all R>=2; legal augmented instances with positive seed weights; C0 in the physical output-label basis.
costs: Exact entry formula uses O(M^2 R) local algebraic operations per requested block entry. Row listing requires at least ceil(5^R/D) outputs. BMVZ has polynomial D and R=n^Omega(1), making this superpolynomial.
evidence: Exact tensor row and bilinear transform in complement_lcu/03_decisive_counterexample.md; rational finite fixture verify_seed_reflection_transition.py.
boundary: Only the canonical projector is ruled out. The seed augmentation is a hardness-preserving admissible family but not proven to lie in the fixed published ABN-to-BMVZ map.

claim: For the specified direct term-frame and active-flag isometries on the augmented seed family, every positive contraction with that exact image kernel and maximum row degree s has normalized gap bounded by a Chebyshev row-mass expression that tends to zero for polynomial s and polynomially growing R.
quantifiers: The fixed isometries and stated seed branch weights; arbitrary positive exact-kernel enforcer C with 0<=C<=I.
costs: The row-mass witness has mass m=1/16 and max selected entry square a=(1/16)8^-R; polynomial output degree forces vanishing normalized gap.
boundary: This does not transfer to complement LCU, whose branch blocks are combinations of the violation projectors rather than the same decoder-unitary transitions.

claim: When H<=3I/4 and Y=I-H=K0, the operator Cinc=T*T/16 with Tz=(z_a-K_aY^-1 z0)_(a>0) has kernel ran(V), lies between 0 and I, and obeys Cinc >= (1/16)(I-VV*).
quantifiers: Every exact complement-LCU isometry whose zero-output block Y is invertible with Y>=I/4.
costs: Exact gap is at least 1/16; matrix blocks use K_aY^-1. No efficient computational row oracle or polynomial row bound is proved.
boundary: This proves an algebraic alternative only; row sparsity/access remains UNKNOWN.

claim: A constant-gap bounded-degree unitary-frame expander connection anchored at the two forced seed reflection frames must contain an edge relative unitary with superpolynomial row support, even allowing global intermediate unitary frames.
quantifiers: Term-anchored unitary-frame connection graph with polynomial vertex count, constant graph gap, and the two seed endpoint frames.
costs: A path has O(log K) edges; relative support multiplication and the seed transition lower bound force edge support exp(Omega(R/log K)).
boundary: Does not cover arbitrary positive enforcers, nonunitary graph relations, active redesigned isometries, or global label-mixing constructions.

claim: For the fixed finite BJSW local projector alphabet, every row of VV* for complement LCU has an epsilon-approximation in l2 supported on poly(M,1/epsilon) entries, uniformly in repetition R and PREPARE completion.
quantifiers: Fixed finite local projector alphabet with uniform rho<1 for every multi-entry local row of Q or QQ'; arbitrary exact PREPARE completion.
costs: Support is O(M^3 d^t0) for constant local support cap d and t0=O(log(M/epsilon)/log(1/rho)).
boundary: Approximate sparsity is not exact row sparsity; it explains why the earlier constant-mass row-witness does not establish a general LCU gap lower bound.

claim: Any scalar polynomial or rational function of the canonical projection C0 that preserves its exact kernel is a scalar multiple of C0 and cannot change its row support.
quantifiers: C0^2=C0, f defined at 0 and 1, f(0)=0 and f(1)>0.
costs: No additional support cost; the fixed-completion 5^R row or completion-independent ceil(5^R/D) lower survives.
boundary: Does not rule out an enforcer not obtained as a scalar function of C0.

claim: Whether the complement-LCU image admits any positive contraction C with exact kernel ran(V), a size-independent full-space gap under ||C||<=1, and a polynomial maximum row support plus efficient row-list oracle.
quantifiers: The full legal augmented BMVZ family and the explicit complement-LCU image; arbitrary C, not necessarily a function of C0 or a connection Laplacian.
costs: The incidence form gives a constant-gap candidate but row access depends on Y^-1. The image also has an O(D)-support kernel relation, defeating a generic minimum-distance proof.
boundary: No positive construction or unrestricted impossibility theorem is established.

claim: The commuting-operator threshold repetition tail, including zero-spectrum operator Jensen and mixed exposure, is a separate game-theoretic result and does not by itself yield the finite-dimensional LCU row oracle or a common positive Hamiltonian encoding.
quantifiers: As stated in the prior Cycle-2 L02 reconstruction and operator exposure audit; details remain in that separate artifact.
costs: No costs or verifier-to-Hamiltonian conversion are inferred in Cycle 3.
boundary: Do not conflate commuting-operator verifier access with finite matrix row-list access or QMA/qPCP constructions.
